item: DuckDB's FATAL allocation error at the edge of its limit is declined as the limit and kept, not retried as a plain failure (R160)
summary: Two of three 20 M-mention builds at 1,004 MB died in the stage insert with a DuckDB FatalException (checkpoint could not allocate a block, 957.3 of 957.4 MiB used) rather than OutOfMemoryException, so the build ended as a plain failure with no kept stop and the next serve request could start the same scan again. A FatalException whose text holds the one fixed phrase 'could not allocate' (matched where it is raised, never stored, logged or chained) is now a duckdb-limit stop at the stage it was in (stage-insert, aggregate or keywords), naming the sizes read before it and engine_error_class FatalException, class name only; the instance is not reused or retried, and the kept stop is released by the rules a duckdb-limit stop already has. Any other FatalException stays a plain failure.
